correctness.rationale: For each existing nontrivial S(2,k,n), pair counting gives r(k-1)=n-1, bk=nr and r>=k, so n>=k(k-1)+1>2k and n>=7. The complement of each k-point block has >k points, hence a noncollinear basis triple and zero minimum of x(B); a basis with two points in the block and one outside gives maximum 2. Coordinate minima/maxima are 0,1. The rank-three matroid basis-exchange proof is valid, and Edmonds rank inequalities reduce the complete polytope to x(E)=3, 0<=x_i<=1, x(B)<=2. For reflected inclusion y=((s+1)c-x)/s, coordinate extrema force 1/(s+1)<=c_i<=s/(s+1). Block maximum y(B) from min x(B)=0 forces c(B)<=2s/(s+1). The lower c(B)>=2/(s+1) in the source is redundant but valid, following from the coordinate lower bounds because k>=3; it is not an independent necessary block-facet constraint. Summing coordinate and block constraints over the regular design yields four lower bounds (n-3)/3, 3/(n-3), 3k/(2n-3k), (2n-3k)/(3k). At the uniform center c=3*1/n all constraints hold for s equal to their maximum, so optimization over arbitrary centers is exact. For k=3, n=7 gives 9/5, and n>=9 gives (n-3)/3; for k>=4, n>=3k+1 implies (n-3)(2n-3k)>=9k. Thus the only exception is Fano. Non-Fano optimality saturates all coordinate lower bounds, forcing c_i=3/n; Fano optimality saturates all seven block upper bounds and A^T A=2I+J is invertible, again forcing c=3*1/n. Independent exact tests checked PG(2,2), AG(2,3), PG(2,3) with 28,72,234 bases and rational reflected containment, as well as 39,200 pairs (n,k) in a finite parameter box for the bound comparison. These finite checks are corroboration only; universal claim follows from algebra and matroid polytope characterization.
residual_risks: The lower block-sum bound is redundant; the source proof speaks as if it came from the block inequality, but the equivalence remains correct because coordinate nonnegativity entails it.
Finite checks validate three designs, not all Steiner designs; no design existence inferred from parameter feasibility.
No claim about arbitrary rank-three matroids, metric ellipsoids, or non-Steiner paving matroids.

value.rationale: The rank-three base polytopes of Steiner systems are a natural, broad design-theoretic class including projective and affine planes and nonisomorphic Steiner triple systems. Their affine-invariant reflection asymmetry and minimizing-center locus are intrinsic geometric invariants not determined by the published Ehrhart/face-vector data. This exact all-design classification shows a stable hypersimplex benchmark despite loss of permutation automorphism symmetry and isolates the seven-point Fano plane as a genuine exceptional boundary. Rigidity of the uniform center is nontrivial when automorphisms need not be transitive. The exact factor and unique center are useful standalone geometry, not merely a known-table value or one-off finite computation.
residual_risks: No classification of generic rank-three matroids or quantitative stability under design perturbations is supplied or required.
The four-bound optimization is short after known Edmonds inequalities and symmetry incidence counting; the substantive mathematical point is its uniform exact classification and Fano anomaly.
